claim_verdicts.evidence: glossary/kube-proxy.md: 'kube-proxy is a network proxy that runs on each node in your cluster'. virtual-ips.md: 'Each instance of kube-proxy watches the Kubernetes control plane for the addition and removal of Service and EndpointSlice objects. For each Service, kube-proxy calls appropriate APIs ... to configure the node to capture traffic to the Service's clusterIP and port, and redirect that traffic to one of the Service's endpoints'.

endpoint-slices.md: 'The control plane automatically creates EndpointSlices for any Kubernetes Service that has a selector specified. These EndpointSlices include references to all the Pods that match the Service selector.' Conditions: 'The three conditions are serving, terminating, and ready.' Ownership: 'a kubernetes.io/service-name label that enables simple lookups of all EndpointSlices belonging to a Service.'

endpoint-slices.md: 'Service proxies will normally ignore endpoints that are terminating, but they may route traffic to endpoints that are both serving and terminating if all available endpoints are terminating.' Round 2: s.4 'A Pod that is not ready normally has no entry' and summary 2 'normally only ready addresses get new connections' now carry the condition.

Captured output (stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/kube-proxy.txt): 'mode: iptables'. kind.sigs.k8s.io home page (WebFetch): 'kind is a tool for running local Kubernetes clusters using Docker container "nodes".' Supports s.5 'Each node of the kind cluster is a Docker container, so docker exec donhang-worker runs iptables-save on that node'.

virtual-ips.md iptables mode: 'it installs a series of iptables rules which redirect from the virtual IP address to more iptables rules, defined per Service. The per-Service rules link to further rules for each backend endpoint, and the per-endpoint rules redirect traffic (using destination NAT) to the backends.' Captured output shows KUBE-SERVICES -d .../32 --dport 80 -j KUBE-SVC-..., two KUBE-SVC -> KUBE-SEP jumps, two KUBE-SEP DNAT --to-destination ...:8080.

Captured output: '-A KUBE-SVC-CLMCAZ67BDWMELKC -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.50000000000 -j KUBE-SEP-...' followed by '-A KUBE-SVC-CLMCAZ67BDWMELKC -j KUBE-SEP-...' (no match condition). With two endpoints this gives each ~1/2. Docs: rules 'by default, select a backend Pod at random'.

virtual-ips.md: 'When a client connects to the Service's virtual IP address the iptables rule kicks in. A backend is chosen (either based on session affinity or randomly)'. kube-proxy.md flag --conntrack-max-per-core: 'Maximum number of NAT connections to track per CPU core' (kernel connection record). Captured: 'answers: 10, different Pods that answered: 1' (one nc connection); 'different Pods that answered: 2' (ten wget).

virtual-ips.md: 'kube-proxy configures packet forwarding rules using the iptables API of the kernel netfilter subsystem' and 'packets are redirected to the backend without rewriting the client IP address'. Note: the quote in source_hint ('without the need to switch between userspace and the kernel space') is not in the mirrored page. glossary/kube-proxy.md adds 'Otherwise, kube-proxy forwards the traffic itself' - so the claim holds for iptables mode only.

RFC 9112 s.9.3: 'HTTP/1.1 defaults to the use of "persistent connections", allowing multiple requests and responses to be carried over a single connection.' s.9.6: 'Connection: close as a request header field indicates that this is the last request that the client will send on this connection' and 'A server that receives a "close" connection option MUST initiate closure of the connection ... after it sends the final response'.
